subject: Follow-up & next steps: technical deep dive + dedicated capacity sizing
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ruth Jensen <ruth.jensen@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & next steps: technical deep dive + dedicated capacity sizing

Hi Ruth — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

TL;DR:
- Ledgerly is a fit for Redwood Dedicated for the use cases you described (real-time document processing + chat).
- Next step: schedule a technical deep dive + dedicated capacity sizing session (throughput/latency-focused).

Recap of what we heard from your team:
- Peak production traffic: ~1,200 concurrent users during business hours, average session ~15 requests.
- Typical request: 350 tokens in, expecting ~450 tokens out.
- Target 95th pct latency for generation: <= 400ms for interactive flows; batch scoring can be higher.
- Data residency: US-only for production; SOC2 required (we covered this in the call).

What we propose for the next meeting:
1) Technical deep dive (60–75m) — we bring our inference SE (Marcus) to validate workload profile, token shapes, cache opportunities, and to capture KV cache guidance.
2) Dedicated sizing session (45–60m) — run through throughput/latency targets, expected QPS patterns, and reserve a GPU pool window.

Proposed windows (Pacific):
- Tue 15 Dec: 09:00–11:00 or 14:00–16:00 PT
- Wed 16 Dec: 10:30–12:00 PT
- Thu 17 Dec: 13:00–15:00 PT

If you prefer, we can split into two meetings (deep dive then sizing) or combine into one 90-minute block. Please let us know which option and which slot works best.

Pre-call asks (to help Marcus prepare):
- Share a representative load snapshot (CSV or export) for a weekday peak hour — QPS/time, token distribution, percent of long tail requests.
- Any infra constraints we should know (VPC peering lead times, approved cloud regions, firewall egress rules).

I've attached a short pre-call checklist we use to speed the sizing conversation. Once we lock a slot I'll send a calendar invite and the mutual action plan link.

Thanks — looking forward to locking something in.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: redwood-precall-checklist.pdf (PDF, 28KB)]

From: Ruth Jensen <ruth.jensen@ledgerly.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@ledgerly.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps: technical deep dive + dedicated capacity sizing

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear recap. We'd like to proceed. A few quick notes and availability: 

Availability: Wed 16 Dec 10:30–12:00 PT works best for our engineering lead (Amit) and product (me). If you can hold that window, we'll accept.

Sharing a brief snapshot now — this is a redacted extract for the peak hour on Nov 18: 
- avg QPS: 420
- 95th token length (in+out): 820 tokens
- 99th latency today (our current infra, not Redwood): ~950ms
- bursts up to 1,100 QPS for short 5–10 minute spikes

Attached: ledgerly-load-snapshot.csv (contains per-minute QPS for the sample hour and token distribution).

Procurement loop: I've CC'd procurement@ledgerly.com (Sara) because we may need to discuss reserved pool terms if we move to Dedicated. We'll handle redlines once the sizing is known.

See you on the 16th — please send an invite and any additional prep.

Best,
Ruth
Head of Product | Ledgerly
[Attachment: ledgerly-load-snapshot.csv (CSV, 42KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ruth Jensen <ruth.jensen@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps: technical deep dive + dedicated capacity sizing

Ruth — great, we’ll mark Wed 16 Dec 10:30–12:00 PT tentatively. I want to propose an agenda to make the session efficient: 

Agenda (90m combined session, or we can split):
- 0–10m: Introductions & goals (Sofia)
- 10–40m: Workload review — Marcus walks the Ledgerly load snapshot and token distributions.
- 40–70m: Sizing exercise — Marcus/SE run estimated GPU footprint, autoscale/burst plan, and recommended quantization/profile.
- 70–85m: Operational considerations — VPC, peering, KMS, monitoring & runbook.
- 85–90m: Next steps & mutual action plan (pricing, RD, legal).

Pre-reads: Marcus and I will review the CSV you attached. Marcus — can you prepare an initial sizing sketch (ballpark GPUs + expected QPS per GPU) and a short run-of-show for the workshop?

Ruth — I'll drop a calendar invite for 16 Dec 10:30 PT now (please accept when convenient). Also linking our mutual action plan in the invite so procurement has visibility.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Hi Ruth/Sofia — I'll run the technical deep dive and sizing exercise next week. A couple of quick asks so the session is productive: 

1) If you can, please add a short column in the CSV that flags example request types (e.g., "interactive-chat", "batch-score"). That helps us map caching and batching strategies.
2) Share any SLOs per endpoint if they differ from the global 95th target you mentioned.

I'll prepare a preliminary sizing sketch based on the CSV you shared and bring two scenarios: conservative (headroom for spikes) and cost-optimized. Expect an initial GPU footprint estimate in the invite notes by EOD Monday.

I'll also attach a one-page pre-call checklist to the calendar invite to make the workshop run faster. Please accept the calendar invite when you get it.

Looking forward —
Marcus Lin
Principal Inference SE | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
